situation: Half the class did the reading and half clearly did not, and the half that did is getting visibly annoyed at carrying discussions.

dims.SPEAKABILITY: Card 1's lines ("came in loaded and ready," "run on half the fuel") sound like a real teacher talking, while Card 2's Collaboration turn ("what would make it more likely that everyone actually shows up ready?") risks opening a soft negotiation that undercuts the standard.
dims.SPECIFICITY: Card 1 diagnoses the precise mechanic — that visible frustration makes it harder for non-readers to re-enter without losing face — whereas Card 2 leans on more portable framing about resentment and belonging.
dims.TIGHTNESS: Card 1 delivers a concrete two-minute pair-talk with assigned roles, while Card 2 repeats "your people in this room matter" beats and asks open questions that pad the moment.
dims.HONESTY: Both hold the reading standard, but Card 1 keeps the discomfort in the room ("both groups know which they are") without offering an escape, while Card 2's invitation to co-design norms risks diluting the immediate cost non-readers should feel.
